candidates.title: PAR validation warning apparatus (single-variant `ParWarning` enum + single-field `ParValidationReport`) is built then discarded at its only production caller

evidence.reading: `ParWarning` has exactly one variant (`LowResidualVariance`) and `ParValidationReport` is a one-field wrapper `{ warnings: Vec<ParWarning> }` — a structured warning taxonomy with a single inhabitant, the textbook wrapper-enum-with-one-inhabitant shape. The apparatus is production-unread: `git grep -nE '\bvalidate_par_parameters\b' a136840d -- 'crates/**/*.rs'` shows the sole production caller is `crates/cobre-stochastic/src/context.rs:616`, `let _report = validate_par_parameters(system.inflow_models())?;` — the return value is bound to `_report` and discarded, so only the fatal `?` path (the std==0 && ar_order>0 error at validation.rs:120) is used and the `warnings` branch (`warnings.push(ParWarning::LowResidualVariance {..})` at validation.rs:138) is computed then dropped. `git grep -nE '\bParWarning\b' a136840d` shows no non-test consumer anywhere except the definition, the `par/mod.rs`/`lib.rs` re-exports, and the internal producer; only `validation.rs`'s own inline `#[cfg(test)]` module inspects `.warnings`. The many `.warnings()` hits in cobre-cli/io/python/sddp are the unrelated `ValidationContext` diagnostic mechanism, not `ParValidationReport`. The doc comment 'The calling algorithm may inspect them ...' is speculative future-tense with no wiring. Reserved-is-not-dead check: not in prior-register.md, not in reserved-seams-and-deferred-debt.md, not covered by CLAUDE.md 'unwired config is reserved' (this is a warning apparatus, not config), and carries no `#[allow(dead_code)]` anchor (tests keep it live) — so no sanction applies.
evidence.reserved_check: cleared: absent from prior-register.md and the mirror; not config (CLAUDE.md reserved-config rule N/A); no #[allow] rationale anchors it

candidates.fixShape: Collapse the single-inhabitant taxonomy: either (a) if the low-residual-variance diagnostic has no intended reader, drop the `warnings` accumulation and return the fatal-check outcome directly (the sole caller already discards it), retiring `ParWarning`, `ParValidationReport`, and the two re-exports; or (b) if the warning is meant to surface, replace the one-variant enum with the bare `LowResidualVariance { hydro_id, stage_id, explained_variance }` struct and actually consume it at context.rs (which, under the Python-parity rule, would require mirroring the surfaced warning in cobre-python — an owner call, not a drive-by). Keep the enum form only if a second warning variant is genuinely imminent, in which case record it as an intended extension seam rather than leaving it as silent debt. No L1-purity conflict: the fix introduces no engine noun, no engine-crate dependency, and removes surface rather than adding a single-consumer abstraction.

candidates.title: Bare `estimate_ar_coefficients` / `estimate_correlation` / `estimate_seasonal_stats` are pub forwarding shims over their `_with_season_map` twins with zero production consumers (only the crate's own tests + doctests)

evidence.reading: Each bare form is a pure forwarding shim: `estimate_ar_coefficients` (ar_coefficients.rs:88) and `estimate_seasonal_stats` (seasonal_stats.rs:221 -> `estimate_seasonal_stats_with_season_map(.., None)`) and `estimate_correlation` (correlation.rs:115 -> `estimate_correlation_with_season_map(.., None)`) do nothing but call their `_with_season_map` twin with `None`. Two of the three are re-exported at the crate root (lib.rs:47: `estimate_ar_coefficients, estimate_seasonal_stats`) and all three at `par::fitting::`. `git grep -nE '\bestimate_ar_coefficients\(' a136840d -- 'crates/**/*.rs' | grep -vE 'estimate_ar_coefficients_with'` (and the analogous greps for the other two) returns only: their own definitions, their own doctests, and the crate's inline `par/fitting/tests.rs` — no production caller inside or outside cobre-stochastic. The one production PAR consumer, cobre-io `scenarios/estimation.rs:65-68`, imports and calls only the `_with_season_map` forms (`estimate_seasonal_stats_with_season_map`, `estimate_correlation_with_season_map`) plus `estimate_ar_coefficients_with_selection`/`ArEstimationConfig`. So the bare trio is public forwarding surface whose only exercisers are the crate's own tests/doctests — a zero-external-consumer forwarding abstraction on an L1 kernel. Reserved-is-not-dead check: none of the three appears in prior-register.md or the mirror; they are wired (to tests) so no `#[allow(dead_code)]` fires; the CLAUDE.md reserved-config rule does not apply (functions, not config). No sanction.
evidence.reserved_check: cleared: absent from prior-register.md and the mirror; wired only to tests/doctests so no dead_code seam; not config

candidates.fixShape: Remove the ergonomic overload asymmetry: since `_with_season_map` already takes `Option<&SeasonMap>` and is the sole production entry, either demote the three bare forwarders to `pub(crate)` (or delete them and have the inline tests/doctests call the `_with_season_map` form with `None` directly), and stop re-exporting `estimate_ar_coefficients`/`estimate_seasonal_stats` at the crate root. If the no-season-map convenience form is deliberately part of the crate's public API, mark that intent explicitly and keep exactly one such surface rather than a crate-root re-export plus a `par::fitting::` re-export of a test-only shim. Behaviour-neutral (the shims already delegate); blast radius is validation-free (the shim bodies and their test/doctest call sites).

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/lag_kernel.rs — `LagIndex` trait with `LagMajor` and `EntityMajor` implementors driving the generic `advance_lag_chain<L: LagIndex>`
positives.why: Not speculative generality: both implementors have real production consumers, so the trait is a genuine two-consumer abstraction (satisfies the target-layering 'second consumer precedes the abstraction' rule). `LagMajor` is used in production by cobre-sddp `src/stochastic/noise.rs:250-251`; `EntityMajor` by cobre-stochastic `sampling/eta_inversion.rs:143`, `sampling/external.rs:2959,3033`, `sampling/historical.rs:2254,2327`, and `par/lag_transition.rs:1268`. Static-dispatched (`impl LagIndex`), never `Box<dyn>`, per the crate hard rule.
positives.sanctionedBy: target-layering-brief.md §3.4 (a two-consumer abstraction is architecture, not a one-consumer smell)

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/fitting/estimation.rs — `ArEstimationConfig<'a>` (line 179) and `PacfReductionParams` (line 1002) parameter-bundle structs
positives.why: These are the sanctioned fix FOR argument-count pressure, not over-engineering: `ArEstimationConfig` bundles the four estimation knobs behind the single public `estimate_ar_coefficients_with_selection` entry that cobre-io actually calls (scenarios/estimation.rs:246,335), and `PacfReductionParams` bundles the reduction controls threaded into `iterative_pacf_reduction`. Collapsing them would re-introduce the too-many-arguments smell, not remove one.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par — newtype / unused-generic census
positives.why: No forwarding tuple-struct newtypes exist in par (`git grep -nE 'pub struct [A-Za-z0-9_]+\(' a136840d -- crates/cobre-stochastic/src/par/` returns empty). The only non-lifetime generic in par is `advance_lag_chain<L: LagIndex>`, and `L` is instantiated at both `LagMajor` and `EntityMajor` in production, so there is no unused generic parameter.
